title: INT8 autocalibration shadow pipeline and golden-answer supplement for weight-only GPTQ/AWQ
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Build an automated shadow/evaluation pipeline that runs INT8 weight-only quantized variants (GPTQ and AWQ) in parallel with FP16 baselines to surface per-request numerical regressions and guide an autocalibration flow. This ticket covers orchestration, telemetry schema, golden-answer diffing, and the automated micro-calibration loop that can be run as a nightly/regression job or on-demand for canaries.

Scope and deliverables: 
- Shadow runner that accepts the same inference traffic samples used by runtime smoke tests and produces side-by-side outputs for FP16 baseline, GPTQ INT8, and AWQ INT8 variants. It must preserve input randomness seeds and track model version.
- Golden-answer delta metric: token-level and answer-level diffs (exact match, embedding cosine, BLEU-like score for long form). Produce both per-request deltas and aggregate metrics with confidence intervals.
- Per-layer drift telemetry: collect per-layer scale/zero-point deltas and activation distributions for problematic samples to aid calibration diagnostics.
- Autocalibration loop prototype: an automated routine that suggests per-layer calibration adjustments (e.g., clip thresholds, per-channel scales) and re-evaluates on the shadow runner to measure improvement. Must be restartable and idempotent.
- Regression integration: wire the shadow pipeline into nightly CI and a weekly long-run fidelity sweep. Provide pass/fail gate thresholds and a human-review workflow for false positives.
- Canary/fallback playbook: define rollout controls that will let runtime fallback to FP16 or alternate quant profile when drift exceeds thresholds.
- Documentation: runbook and a Confluence doc with examples, data retention rules, and query recipes for Console dashboards.

Non-goals: retraining of weights, production in-path inference changes, or creating new quant formats beyond GPTQ/AWQ.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Shadow pipeline ingests sample traffic and outputs side-by-side artifacts into the regression S3 bucket within latency bounds (nightly budget).
- Golden-answer delta computes and stores summary metrics; nightly job fails if high-severity regressions (answer-level regressions above configured threshold) are detected.
- Telemetry shows per-layer signals for failing samples that are human-actionable (at least two top contributing layers reported).
- Autocalibration run produces a recommended calibration file and a delta report showing measurable reduction in regression score for at least 80% of failing queries in the debug dataset.
- PR with implementation + unit tests merged and an accompanying Console dashboard prototype linked in attachments.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow outputs generated for baseline + GPTQ + AWQ for provided sample set
Nightly regression job runs and gates on golden-answer delta thresholds
Per-layer telemetry surfaced and queryable in Console
Autocalibration recommendations reduce regression score for >=80% of failing queries in debug set
Canary fallback playbook documented and linked
comments: 2025-01-11 - Kickoff: scoped project with Research and Runtime. Agreed sampling window: 10k requests sampled across 24h traffic for nightly sweep.
2025-01-18 - Design review: Sofia Martinez (Research) and Priya Patel (Runtime) requested adding per-channel scale logging to telemetry; accepted with follow-up to bound storage cost.

2025-01-24 - Early prototype: shadow runner written as a shim that forks requests to an offline runner; initial artifacts landed in s3://redwood-regressions/eng-629013/prototype/, see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/8172

2025-01-30 - Telemetry schema update: added fields sample_id, seed, seq_len, model_variant, layer_scale_map (sparse map), and numeric_summary (min/max/mean/std). Draft schema in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/629013-shadow-telemetry-schema

2025-02-05 - Autocalibration PoC: ran on 500 debug queries; reduced median token-delta by 22% for GPTQ variant but introduced small regression on 7% of queries. Decided to gate recommendations behind manual review for first month.
2025-02-12 - PM review (Evan Brooks): requested addition of a canary SLO threshold and an automated rollback flag. Added to acceptance criteria and canary playbook.

2025-02-14 - Engineering update: integrated nightly job into CI with smoke test; still tuning storage TTL for per-layer telemetry (cost estimate TBD). Pending: formal security review and export control sign-off.
